expectation: Membrane/cytoplasmic stain on macrophages (and some DCs, endothelium): a moderately common population of scattered single irregular cells in the lamina propria, submucosa and serosa. Many overlap CD163; vessels may show faint lining.
observed: A: scattered punctate cells across the submucosa/muscle-adjacent zones of both sections, plus diffuse mucosal haze. B/C: haze, with puncta lining the epithelial edge. D: one irregular, ringed cell. E: many CD206 cells sit on CD163 cells (white), plus some green-only puncta.
why: Discrete, irregular macrophage-like cells are scattered through the stroma, and in row E they co-localise extensively with CD163 cells, as the marker graph says they should.
notes: There is a clear CD206 population of irregular stromal cells, largely overlapping CD163 in row E. There is also mucosal haze and puncta along the epithelial edge that may be background, but the cellular overlap with CD163 is convincing.
